summary: This bill requires the Postal Service to sell a Combating Invasive Species Semipostal Stamp for two years, with the surcharge proceeds split equally between the Departments of the Interior and Agriculture to fund their invasive-species programs.

scores.thoughts: The bill authorizes a semipostal stamp whose differential proceeds are transferred to DOI and USDA programs that combat invasive species. This creates a voluntary revenue stream that will increase federal spending on those specific programs, though the amounts involved are modest and not drawn from general revenues or mandatory appropriations. The effect is therefore a minor expansion of government spending.
The legislation contains no provisions altering tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue collection mechanisms. It relies solely on voluntary stamp purchases rather than taxation.
No provisions relate to healthcare delivery, insurance, public coverage, or market-based reforms.
The bill does not address firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No content pertains to immigration pathways, border enforcement, or related protections.
The legislation is silent on reproductive health services or abortion access.
No references to defense budgets, military programs, or national security spending.

The bill explicitly funds programs at DOI and USDA to combat invasive species, which the findings describe as threats to ecosystems and native species. This directly supports expanded environmental protection and restoration activities.
No provisions affect welfare programs, food assistance, or other safety-net entitlements.
The bill does not address schools, federal education funding, or school-choice policies.
No content relates to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled-substance regulation.
The legislation contains nothing on sentencing, policing, rehabilitation, or criminal-justice reform.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
While the stamp generates some dedicated revenue, the amounts are negligible relative to the federal budget and do not meaningfully alter deficit or debt trajectories.
The bill does not engage with LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil-rights issues.
No provisions concern foreign assistance or international aid programs.
The legislation is unrelated to voting access, election administration, or voter-ID requirements.
No content addresses technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
The bill contains no labor, union, or workplace provisions.
No provisions touch on religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
